summary: IDS s060_single is degraded due to oversize frames: 4.8% of frames (157/3292, up to 8058 bytes) exceed the IDS 1G port MTU of 1518 bytes and are dropped by the NIC, creating detection blind spots. No other visibility faults detected.

findings.root_cause: Network path is carrying jumbo frames (observed up to 8058 bytes) while the IDS tool port is standard 1518-byte Ethernet only. The packet broker is forwarding them unchanged, so the IDS NIC drops them at ingress as oversize/invalid.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently drops ~4.8% of frames before inspection. As this IDS needs full payload for signature matching, those flows are not inspected, allowing potential evasions and reducing detection coverage.

params.target: IDS port and packet broker egress toward IDS

recommended_fix.why: Tool requires full payload so slicing/trimming to 1518 bytes is not an option. Must increase MTU capability on the IDS NIC (enable jumbo frames to 9000/9216) and ensure broker egress MTU matches, or normalize MTU upstream to <=1518 if jumbo is not intended. This prevents NIC-level drops without losing payload needed for detection.
